4th Period.workingNow: Linking your first CSS stylesheet and changing your page's font and colors.
4th Period.weeklyDeliverable: Your About Me page with an external CSS stylesheet linked — custom fonts/colors, class/ID selectors, padding/margin, and an organized layout — pushed and ready to submit Sunday night.
4th Period.smartGoal: I can link a CSS stylesheet to my HTML page so that I can start customizing how it looks.
4th Period.contentStandard: CA CS Standards 6-8.AP.13 — Create prototypes using structured code, organized into separate linked pages, to fulfill a design requirement.
4th Period.eldStandard: ELD.PI.6-8.5 — Listening actively to spoken English in a range of social and academic contexts.
agenda: Log in (timed) (2 min)
Quick overview: today's plan (3 min)
I do: what is CSS? Model linking a stylesheet + changing one color (10 min)
We do: change the page's font together as a class (8 min)
You do: link your own stylesheet, change your body font and one color (22 min)
Exit Ticket: paste your <link> tag (5 min)
4th Period.connections: Last week you finished your About Me page's HTML content — structure, text, an image, and a table. Starting today we go super slow through CSS, one new idea a day, so by Sunday your page won't just have content, it'll have style.

6th Period.workingNow: Finding a partner, then joining another pair to form your group of four for this week's game plan.
6th Period.weeklyDeliverable: A group platformer game plan (character states, at least one obstacle/enemy state, and a labeled level sketch) created in groups of four.
6th Period.smartGoal: I can join a group of four and brainstorm platformer game ideas so that my group has a shared direction to plan around.
6th Period.contentStandard: CA CS Standards 6-8.AP.10 — Use flowcharts and/or pseudocode to design solutions to complex problems.
6th Period.eldStandard: ELD.PI.6-8.1 — Exchanging information and ideas with others through collaborative discussions.
agenda: Log in (timed) (2 min)
Quick overview: today's plan (3 min)
Find a partner, then get randomly paired with another pair — groups of 4 (5 min)
I do: what makes a platformer game fun? quick examples (5 min)
We do: brainstorm one platformer idea together as a class (5 min)
You do: as a group, brainstorm 2-3 platformer game ideas and pick one (25 min)
Share out: one group shares their idea (5 min)
6th Period.connections: Last week you finished your three-state game and embedded it on your website. This week is different — you won't be coding at all. Instead, in groups of four, you'll spend the whole week planning a more ambitious platformer game, using the state machine ideas you already know as your foundation.
